evidence: '...signed into law on July 4, 2025 as Public Law 119-21. [It] amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026.'
'For calendar year 2027, the basic exclusion amount under § 2010(c)(3) is $15,480,000.' Also used for the gift-tax credit and the GST exemption.

source_title: IRS Rev. Proc. 2026-35 and IRS Estate tax table (ratio)

evidence: 'For calendar year 2027, the first $20,000 of gifts to any person (other than gifts of future interests in property) are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts'.

item: Portability of a deceased spouse's unused exclusion
value: Available by election on a timely filed estate tax return
evidence: 'estates of decedents survived by a spouse may elect to pass any of the decedent's unused exemption to the surviving spouse. This election is made on a timely filed estate tax return'.

item: What counts in the gross estate
value: Fair market value at death of everything owned, including real estate and trusts
evidence: 'The fair market value of these items is used... The includible property may consist of cash and securities, real estate, insurance, trusts, annuities, business interests and other assets.'

value: Fair market value on the date of death (or alternate valuation date if elected on Form 706)
evidence: 'The basis of property inherited from a decedent is generally... The fair market value (FMV) of the property on the date of the decedent's death (whether or not the executor of the estate files an estate tax return'.
Rates of 0%, 15% and 20% by taxable income; 'unrecaptured section 1250 gain from selling section 1250 real property is taxed at a maximum 25% rate'.
Table: Married Individuals Filing Joint Returns — Maximum Zero Rate Amount $102,100; Maximum 15% Rate Amount $633,600.
Table: All Other Individuals — $51,050 and $563,200.
Table 5 — Estates and Trusts: the 37% rate applies to taxable income over $16,500. Income kept inside a trust reaches the top rate very quickly.

'3.8 percent on the lesser of the net investment income, or the excess of MAGI over ... $250,000 for married filing jointly ... $200,000 for single'. Net investment income includes rents and net gains from real estate.

item: Exclusion of gain on sale of a main home
value: $250,000 (single) / $500,000 (joint); owned and lived in 2 of the last 5 years
evidence: 'exclude up to $250,000 of that gain ... or up to $500,000 ... if you file a joint return'; 'owned the home for at least 24 months (2 years) out of the last 5 years' and used it as a residence for at least 24 months.

source_title: IRS — What's new: Estate and gift tax
evidence: 'Treasury Decision 10055 increased the user fee ... to $76, effective October 26, 2026.' Only relevant if a Form 706 is filed.

item: Depreciation of a residential rental building
value: 27.5 years, straight line (land is not depreciated)
evidence: 'You depreciate the residential rental property under MACRS GDS. This means using the straight line method over a recovery period of 27.5 years.' (official page text as returned by search)

item: Trust assets NOT included in the estate
evidence: 'the basis adjustment under section 1014 generally does not apply to the assets of an irrevocable grantor trust not included in the deceased grantor's gross estate'. A revocable living trust is included in the estate and does get the step-up; the trust type must be confirmed with the attorney. (official page text as returned by search)

value: Gain = sale price minus date-of-death value; reported on Schedule D / Form 8949
evidence: 'If you sell the property for more than your basis, you have a taxable gain.' A sale soon after death, at about the date-of-death value, produces little or no taxable gain.

item: Estate tax return deadline (only if a return is required or portability is elected)
value: 9 months after the date of death; automatic 6-month extension with Form 4768
evidence: 'The Form 706 tax return and tax are due nine months from the date of death, unless Form 4768 ... has been filed'; 'automatic 6-month extension of time to file'. (official page text as returned by search)

item: Income tax return for the trust after the death
value: Form 1041 if the trust or estate has $600 or more of gross income in a year; calendar-year returns due April 15
source_title: IRS — File an estate tax income tax return
evidence: 'If the estate generates more than $600 in annual gross income, you are required to file Form 1041'; 'For calendar year estates and trusts, file Form 1041 and Schedule(s) K-1 on or before April 15 of the following year.' (official page text as returned by search)

item: Tax identification number for the trust after the death
value: A separate EIN is needed before filing Form 1041; apply online, by fax or by mail
source_title: IRS — File an estate tax income tax return
evidence: 'Before you file an estate income tax return, you need a tax identification number for the estate... also called an employer identification number (EIN)'. (official page text as returned by search)

item: Loss on selling a home you live in
evidence: 'Losses from the sale of personal-use property, such as your home or car, aren't tax deductible.'
